- When sentiment is consistently low (0.00–0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% above peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.67) and model forecast is below recent history mean, adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to align with bullish sentiment.
- When sentiment turns negative (0.00) after a peak, model often fails to anticipate downward correction; apply a 1–3% downward bias to forecast tail.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent volatility; apply a 1–3% mean-reversion adjustment toward 14-day rolling average of price.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and forecast is erratic, use sentiment-weighted average of 3–5 prior days to stabilize output.
